u1.title: Finding your way
u1.description: The keyboard, middle {c}, finger numbers and your first melodies.

u2.title: Rhythm with real notes
u2.description: Quarter, half and whole notes, rests and eighth notes.

u3.title: Reading the treble clef
u3.description: The staff, its lines and spaces, landmark notes like middle {c}, and melodies read from the staff.

u4.title: The bass clef and the left hand
u4.description: Landmark notes in the bass clef, left-hand melodies and the grand staff.

u5.title: Hands together
u5.description: Both hands at once: moving the same way and in mirror image, then a melody over bass notes.

u6.title: Chords
u6.description: Major and minor chords, inversions, the I, IV and V chords, and ways to accompany a melody.

u7.title: Scales and fingering
u7.description: The {c} major, {g} major and {f} major scales, with the thumb passing under.

u8.title: Sharps, flats and naturals
u8.description: The black keys’ two names, accidentals in the music, the natural sign, {a} minor and neighbor notes.

u9.title: Touch
u9.description: How each key is played: legato and slurs, staccato, accents, tenuto and ties.

u10.title: The sustain pedal
u10.description: The right pedal: its marks, changing it with each chord, under broken chords, and when to leave it up.

u11.title: Around the keyboard
u11.description: Moving the hands: position shifts, octave jumps, arpeggios in {c}, {g} and {f} major, and one hand crossing over the other.

u12.title: More keys
u12.description: The keys of {d} major and {bFlat} major, the relative minors, the natural and harmonic minor scales of {a}, {e} and {d}, and reading with these key signatures.
